name: Mathematics
boundaries: Mathematics: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: The direct consequence is a square-root error in the prime-counting function and a long list of conditional theorems. Bombieri’s examples include an effective Chebotarev theorem, a cubic-form result, and Miller’s conditional primality test; he does not give a factoring algorithm. Deterministic polynomial-time primality is already unconditional by the AKS theorem. The historical claims of new factoring algorithms, proofs of cryptographic security, and a revolution in error-correcting codes do not follow. Clay still lists the hypothesis as unsolved. That status makes it a central conjecture. It does not make the proof a new general method at the scale used here.

The historical writeup treats both outcomes as one discovery and says that P ≠ NP would protect modern cryptography forever, while P = NP would make drug design and AI training trivially solvable. The first claim needs one-way functions, which are a further question. The second depends on a small exponent and on the problems actually lying in NP. MAT-01 keeps the usable positive algorithm as the revolutionary scope and records the separation as a different theorem.

original_dispositions.original_title: Proof of existence and smoothness for three-dimensional Navier–Stokes
original_dispositions.reason: The predictive capability people attach to this statement is MAT-03, and the attachment is too loose to identify the two. Fefferman’s statements (A) and (B) are zero-force global regularity. (C) and (D) are breakdown with a smooth force. OpenAI claimed (C) and (D) on 8 September 2026. Clay said on 11 September 2026 that the problem had apparently been settled and that review was unhurried. No prize had been awarded by the cutoff. Sreenivasan and Schumacher warn against taking regularity as the definition of the turbulence problem. Accurate long-term weather prediction and wind-tunnel-free aircraft design are not direct consequences of a yes-or-no regularity theorem.

Clay’s overview says it asks how much of the topology of a projective variety is cut out by algebraic equations, and that it is known in special cases, including when the solution set has dimension less than four. A proof would answer that question inside algebraic geometry. Mirror symmetry and string theory would require further arguments. The Clay archive’s note on the 12 November 2025 Deligne lecture says the evidence is limited. Limited evidence is uncertainty about truth, not a reason to promote a classification conjecture into a new calculus.

Andrew Wiles’s official text says a proof of the strong form would give an effective means of finding generators for the rational points. That is a real arithmetic capability, and it is narrower than a new general method. The rank-equals-order statement is known when the analytic rank is 0 or 1, by Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin, and later work recorded in that text. Elliptic-curve cryptography depends on the discrete logarithm, which is part of MAT-06, not on this conjecture. The conjecture also sits beside MAT-02 and is not implied by the correspondence alone. A Zenodo manuscript claiming a complete proof was not treated as a community result.

original_dispositions.original_title: Proof of Yang–Mills existence and the mass gap
original_dispositions.reason: Clay’s public summary says experiment and simulation suggest a mass gap. The official problem asks for a nontrivial quantum theory on four-dimensional space with a spectral gap above the vacuum. Lattice gauge theory already estimates that gap numerically. A construction would make the theory a mathematical object. It would not, by itself, compute new masses, and it would not explain a Proca mass for gluons. The historical sentence about gluons having mass while photons do not misstates the gap. A secondary report updated 28 October 2026 said an OpenAI manuscript claimed existence without the mass gap and that Clay still listed the problem unsolved. I did not inspect that manuscript. Existence without a gap would not meet the prize statement, and neither version meets the capability bar used here.

David Barina reports verification for every starting value below 2^71. The Springer PDF says the project pushed the verified limit from 2^68 to 2^71. Terence Tao proved in 2019 that almost every orbit falls below any function that tends to infinity. The conjecture for every positive integer remains open. A proof would explain one iteration. It would not supply a general method for dynamical systems, computer science, or biology.

Oliveira e Silva, Herzog, and Pardi confirmed the even conjecture for every even number up to 4×10^18. The even statement remains unproved. Verifying an additive pattern to 4×10^18, or proving it for all even integers, does not create a new structure theory beyond what sieve methods and computation already use.

original_dispositions.original_title: Proof of the twin prime conjecture
original_dispositions.reason: Yitang Zhang proved in 2013 that some finite bound on prime gaps occurs infinitely often. Carol Wu records the twin-prime statement as unresolved and records the Polymath8b bound of 246. Preprints from August and September 2026 claim bounds from 240 down to 212; I did not audit them. None of the accepted results, and none of those claims, is a proof that the gap 2 occurs infinitely often. Bounded gaps were the breakthrough. Closing the remaining distance to 2 would complete that theorem. It would not open a new method of the kind already gained from Zhang and Maynard.

original_dispositions.original_title: Proof that no odd perfect number exists, or discovery of one
original_dispositions.reason: Pascal Ochem and Michaël Rao proved that any odd perfect number exceeds 10^1500, has at least 101 prime factors counting multiplicity, and has a largest component above 10^62. No example is known. Euler’s form already constrains any example. Finding one, or proving there is none, would finish a classical question. It would not change the structure of the integers in a way that propagates through mathematics.

reconciliation_change_log.change: 2026-11-11. Initial note. MAT-01 through MAT-08 assigned. Riemann, Hodge, Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer, Yang–Mills, Collatz, Goldbach, twin primes, odd perfect numbers, and Navier–Stokes regularity were examined and left off the list.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Not established in the research notes.

reconciliation_change_log.change: 2026-11-11, revision. All eight identities kept. MAT-01 now states that a separation would not secure public-key cryptography and that satisfiability does not factor integers. MAT-02 now marks Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer as a neighboring conjecture rather than a corollary. MAT-03 now separates regularity from transport and records Fefferman’s own description of the existence gap. MAT-06 now points to MAT-09 and says Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer does not decide elliptic-curve discrete logarithms. MAT-09 added: a usable classical polynomial algorithm for the lattice problems behind ML-KEM. Historical impact claims for the Riemann hypothesis, Navier–Stokes, Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer, and Yang–Mills were checked against Clay problem texts and corrected in the disposition. Three historical survey citations were not found.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The addition is justified by NIST’s 2024 standard, the absence of a polynomial algorithm in Pellet-Mary’s 2024 lecture notes, and the April 2024 withdrawal of a claimed quantum polynomial algorithm for learning with errors.
